# StrixLab — coding-agent guide

StrixLab is pre-alpha, local, CLI-first research tooling for reproducible AMD
Strix Halo optimization experiments. It orchestrates existing runtimes and
isolated native builds and records immutable, verifiable run evidence. It is not
an inference runtime, leaderboard, remote code-execution service, or upstream
patch bot.

## Before changing code

- Read `README.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` first.
- Use `uv`. There is no second task runner and no pre-commit framework.
- Keep changes narrow, evidence-oriented, and independently testable.

## Planned scenarios

- `docs/rocm10-topk-gfx1151.md` fixes the planned ROCm 10 top-k contract and
  CAPSULE-001/TOPK-001 sequence. It is not runnable: do not invent a suite
  manifest or experiment until the documented capsule seam exists.

## Repository validation (no special hardware)

Run this path to validate a clean checkout without any GPU:

```bash
uv sync --locked --all-groups
uv run strixlab --help
uv run pytest
```

Fuller developer checks:

```bash
uv lock --check
uv run ruff format --check .
uv run ruff check .
uv run mypy src
uv run pytest --cov=strixlab --cov-report=term-missing --cov-fail-under=90
uv build
```

## Self-service smoke suite (real Strix Halo only)

The default `configs/builds/hip-rocm-gfx1151.yaml` profile is the installed ROCm
7.2.4 control. ROCm 10 work must use the distinct
`configs/builds/hip-rocm10-gfx1151.yaml` profile and follow
`docs/rocm10-bringup.md`. That lane is provisional, inactive, and not runnable;
do not download, extract, execute, or install ROCm 10, create `/opt/rocm-10`, or
change `/opt/rocm`, alternatives, packages, drivers, or shell startup files.
Activation requires a vendor authenticity anchor or explicit human risk
acceptance plus a separately reviewed isolation plan. It also requires a
separately reviewed, versioned prefix inventory verifier proving staged versus
installed equality and later baseline equality. No such verifier exists in this
branch. A selected environment is not loaded-library proof; attested CMake,
binary-hash, `readelf`, and `ldd` evidence do not hash external ROCm library bytes.

Prerequisites: ROCm at `/opt/rocm`, the pinned GGUF kept outside the repository,
and a credential-clean shell. StrixLab does not download weights. Set `MODELS`
so the file declared by `configs/models/qwen35-4b-smoke.yaml` exists at
`$MODELS/qwen35-4b/Qwen_Qwen3.5-4B-Q4_K_M.gguf` with the declared size and
SHA-256.

Run in this order. Source and build preparation print their IDs on the first
line, model verification prints only the receipt digest, and the suite prints
its ID after `run:`. Copy only the ID or digest—not a label—into the following
assignment instead of using the literal `...`.

```bash
export MODELS=/absolute/path/to/model-root
uv run strixlab doctor --machine configs/machines/strix-halo-128g.yaml

uv run strixlab source prepare configs/sources/strix-llama.yaml
PREPARATION_ID='prep-strix-llama-...'

uv run strixlab build prepare "$PREPARATION_ID" \
  configs/builds/hip-rocm-gfx1151.yaml
BUILD_ID='build-sha256:...'

uv run strixlab model verify configs/models/qwen35-4b-smoke.yaml \
  --source "$PREPARATION_ID"
MODEL_RECEIPT_SHA256='...'

uv run strixlab run suite configs/suites/smoke-qwen35.yaml \
  --machine configs/machines/strix-halo-128g.yaml \
  --build "$BUILD_ID" \
  --model-receipt "$MODEL_RECEIPT_SHA256"
RUN_ID='run-...'

uv run strixlab run inspect "$RUN_ID"
uv run strixlab bundle export "$RUN_ID" "../strixlab-bundle-$RUN_ID"
uv run strixlab bundle verify "../strixlab-bundle-$RUN_ID"
```

Optionally, produce a second equivalent run and compare the two offline with
`strixlab compare BASELINE_RUN_ID CANDIDATE_RUN_ID`, then inspect and export the
comparison run alongside both source runs. The comparison is offline, matched,
conservative, and non-scoring: its no-op result is `inconclusive`, and a comparison
bundle is a derived report that is not independently verifiable without both
source-run bundles. Never present an `inconclusive`, `regression`, or `mixed`
verdict as a failure of the comparison itself, or a comparison as an official score.

Do not work around a failed correctness gate or claim a performance result from
an incomplete run. Report the failure or friction exactly, with secrets and
identifying paths redacted. A successful run is still a provisional field
observation, not an official score or optimization win.

## Field reports

A field report is a small, privacy-safe observation copied from
`field-reports/TEMPLATE.md` to `field-reports/YYYY-MM-DD-<short-slug>.md`. It
records: report kind, StrixLab commit, date and reporter, a machine/OS/GPU
summary without unique host identifiers, the exact commands run (with
repository-relative paths kept but identifying values redacted), a
pass/fail/inconclusive outcome, hardware-run identifiers and verified
bundle-summary fields when available, redacted failure or friction notes, and an
explicit confirmation that no weights, credentials, private data, raw home, or
bundle are included. Failed and inconclusive results are valuable and must be
reported honestly.

## Community experiments

Read `docs/community-workflow.md` before proposing optimization work. Use these
terms precisely:

- scenario: the checked-in suite manifest and its resolved digest;
- candidate: the reproducible change being evaluated;
- run: one local baseline or candidate execution;
- replication: one contributor's matched baseline and candidate attempt, plus
  an offline comparison when both pass correctness;
- experiment: one candidate under one scenario, with one checked-in catalog
  record and potentially many replications.

Propose a new scenario through an Issue before implementing it. Use a scenario
PR for the suite/config contract and one experiment PR per candidate. An
experiment PR may wait in draft form for a GPU owner; do not fabricate hardware
results or replace the correctness gate with repository-only tests. Replications
may be coordinated in PR comments, but accepted summaries must be copied into
`experiments/<scenario-id>/<experiment-id>/README.md` before merge. A candidate
correctness failure is a useful negative replication and must not be forced
through comparison. Later replications use follow-up PRs against the same
record.

Do not call a rerun "validation": verification means checking evidence
integrity, while replication is another observation. Do not call a candidate a
solution or claim `best-known` unless maintainers have assigned that status for
the exact scenario. A merged experiment is cataloged and reproducible, not
universally faster or production-ready.

## Never commit or upload

Model weights, raw StrixLab homes, private data, credentials, or evidence
bundles. Reports carry only small summaries, identifiers, digests, exact
commands, and redacted excerpts.

## Authorization boundaries

Do not push, open a pull request, change any external repository, or claim a
solution, score, or "win" without explicit human authorization. StrixLab
experiments are community-reviewed local observations, not remotely executed
submissions.
